# The grouped block for the first invoice, on a wire whose other settlement
# has since been orphaned by an unpost.
#
# It names the −60.00 and −40.00 that settle this invoice and declares the
# 30.00 left over. Beside them the −50.00 is loose — not because it is residue,
# but because unposting the invoice it settled let it go, and this tool marked
# it as its own orphan when it did.
#
# The writer of every `prepayment:` line skips such a split: an orphan is a
# settlement waiting to be put back, not money the payment left over. A reader
# that counts it makes 80.00 of a 30.00 residue and refuses the export that
# wrote it.
#
# What this fixture produces: both splits applied in this invoice's lot, the
# 30.00 parked as the customer's credit, and the orphan left alone.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-28
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    prepayment: 30
    Transaction "5150aabb5150ccdd5150eeff51500011"
      PaymentSplit "5150aabb5150ccdd5150eeff51500033"
      PaymentSplit "5150aabb5150ccdd5150eeff51500044"
